title: Ashura: two ways
hook: a Sunni fast and a Shia commemoration, each explained by its own people

segments.voice: Yesterday, Muharram, the month the hadith calls Allah's month, where a voluntary fast is praised as the best after Ramadan. Your line: allah's month. Did the day you chose make it onto a calendar? Today, one day inside that month. Day one thousand three hundred fifty-five.

Same date, two rooms. In one kitchen, before dawn, a family is eating quietly so they can fast through the day, thankful for a rescue in the time of Musa. Across town, people dressed in black fill a hall in the evening. Someone recites, slowly, the story of a grandson of the Prophet and the thirst of his family, and people weep. At the door, volunteers hand out cups of water. Both of them are keeping Ashura. Today, the two ways, each in the words its own people use.
screen: `A FAMILY FASTING BEFORE DAWN.` → `A HALL IN BLACK, A STORY RECITED.` → `THE SAME DAY.`

segments.voice: First, the fast, as Sunni Muslims explain it. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps a report from Ibn 'Abbas. When the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, came to Madinah, he found the Jews there fasting on the day of Ashura. He asked why. They told him, in paraphrase: it's a good day, the day Allah saved the Children of Israel from their enemy, so Musa fasted it. And he answered: I have more right to Musa than you. So he fasted it, and told people to fast. A neighbor's fast, recognized and shared. In Sahih Muslim he says he hopes the fast of Ashura wipes away the sins of the year before, and in another report he says that if he lives to the next year, he'll fast the ninth as well. So some Sunni families fast that day along with the day before it. Second, the commemoration, as Shia Muslims explain it. On Ashura, the histories say, Husayn ibn 'Ali, the Prophet's grandson, was killed at Karbala along with members of his family and companions, after days cut off from water. For Shia Muslims, the day is one of mourning. They gather in majalis, gatherings where the story is told and elegies are recited. In some places there are processions. And water is given out, in memory of the thirst at Karbala. Shia speakers describe Husayn's stand as a refusal to bow to injustice, and grief for him as a way of keeping faith with that stand. Third: these aren't strangers to each other's day. Sunni tradition honors Husayn too. A hadith in al-Tirmidhi calls Hasan and Husayn the leaders of the youth of Paradise. Fourth: one date, two ways of keeping it, and each makes sense from inside.
screen: `A FAST FOR MUSA'S RESCUE.` · `A MOURNING FOR HUSAYN AT KARBALA.` · `SUNNIS HONOR HUSAYN TOO.` · `ONE DATE, TWO WAYS.`

segments.voice: The practice: learn how your neighbors keep it. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the two scenes from the start: the quiet kitchen before dawn, and the hall with the cups of water at the door. Spend a few breaths with each, without choosing between them. Then think of one person you could ask, someday, how their family keeps Ashura. A coworker, a neighbor, someone at a mosque. Shape one curious, gentle question you might ask them. Just one. If you pray, you can remember Musa's rescue and Husayn's family together. The bell holds the time.
Ashura. A day in Muharram, kept by Sunni Muslims with a fast for Musa's rescue, and by Shia Muslims as a day of mourning for Husayn at Karbala. Today's word.

Your line: two ways of keeping it. Today, if the question you shaped feels right, ask it, and listen to the whole answer before you say anything. Tomorrow, Rabi' al-Awwal. Day one thousand three hundred fifty-five.

howItsDone: Sunni practice includes a voluntary fast on Ashura, sometimes with the day before it, following hadiths in al-Bukhari and Muslim; Shia Muslims keep Ashura as a day of mourning for Husayn ibn 'Ali at Karbala, with gatherings called majalis, recited elegies, processions in some places, and the giving of water.

fork.setup: the Prophet, newly arrived in Madinah, finds his Jewish neighbors fasting on Ashura. what does he do?
options: asks why, then fasts it himself and tells others to fast.
fork.reveal: he asked, heard it was the day Allah saved the Children of Israel, said he had more right to Musa, and fasted it and told people to fast.

original.note: Arabic: the name of the day in Muharram.

trapdoor: what you thought: Ashura is one holiday everyone keeps the same way.
what it means: one date with two observances: a Sunni fast for Musa's rescue, and a Shia commemoration of Husayn at Karbala.
what a scholar hears: Ibn 'Abbas's report in al-Bukhari and the ninth-day report in Muslim on one side; the majalis and the water of Karbala on the other.
